script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for May 13. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
That sandwich on your plate?  The bread was wheat growing in a field.  The lettuce was leaves absorbing sunlight.

The average American meal travels over 1,500 miles from farm to plate. Apples from New Zealand, fish from Norway, spices from India. Your dinner represents a global network—impressive in scale, invisible in experience. Despite thousands of edible plants, most of the world's food comes from just 12 plant species: wheat, corn, rice, potatoes, and a few others.  Five animal species provide most meat.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Eating is participating in nature's cycles.  Every meal connects you to farms, ecosystems, and other living things.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Food Origin Tracing - Follow the Chain.

Here's your activity: Pick one item from your next meal and trace its origin as far as you can. Where was it grown? How far did it travel? Who touched it along the way? This simple exercise reveals the invisible systems that feed you. This helps you connect food to its sources.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about where food comes from can be applied to food origin tracing - follow the chain. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
